ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure marks four cities participating in the “Earth Hour” activity. On the left figure, Copenhagen, Beijing, and Singapore can be seen; on the right figure, Rio de Janeiro can be seen. Their approximate latitudes are respectively: Copenhagen about 56°N, Beijing about 40°N, Singapore about 1°N, Rio de Janeiro about 23°S. Then reason: the activity date is March 23, 2013, close to the spring equinox. The direct solar point is near the equator and slightly north, and the solar declination is approximately close to 0°. The noon solar altitude formula is H = 90° - |local latitude φ - solar declination δ|. Compare the latitude differences between the four cities and the solar direct latitude: Singapore is closest to the direct solar point, Beijing differs by about 40°, Rio de Janeiro differs by more than about 23°, and Copenhagen differs by more than about 55°. The greater the latitude difference, the smaller the noon solar altitude, therefore among the four cities, the one with the smallest noon solar altitude is Copenhagen.

method.method_draft: First identify the four cities and their approximate latitudes from the map. From the text date 2013年3月23日, infer the solar declination is near the equator, slightly north of 0°. For each city, compare |φ - δ|: Singapore is closest to δ, Rio is about 23° away, Beijing about 40° away, and Copenhagen about 55° away. Since Copenhagen has the greatest latitude distance from the subsolar latitude, its noon solar altitude is the smallest.

Compare the latitude differences between the four cities and the solar direct latitude: Singapore is closest to the direct solar point, Beijing differs by about 40°, Rio de Janeiro differs by more than about 23°, and Copenhagen differs by more than about 55°. The greater the latitude difference, the smaller the noon solar altitude, therefore among the four cities, the one with the smallest noon solar altitude is Copenhagen.
